candidates.excerpt: Police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise following a freight train burglary in Colton, California. Officers spotted a black Chevrolet Silverado leaving the area and initiated a traffic stop. The investigation ended with one arrest and 350 boxes of toy cars in police custody. According to video released by the Colton Police Department, the caller reported people stealing merchandise near Maple Street. An officer positioned himself near Seventh Street and La Cadena Drive while monitoring the surrounding roads. Footage shows authorities following the pickup before stopping its driver. The man exited with his hands on his head, and officers took him into custody. The department confirmed the recovery in its October 22 Facebook announcement. candidates.title: Commissioners approve new rail line to Port of Moses Lake, Wash.
candidates.excerpt: MOSES LAKE, Wash. — Port of Moses Lake commissioners have approved a contract to build a new rail line connecting the port to the Columbia Basin Railroad. The Hagadone News Network reports that commissioners approved a $31.75 million contract with Martinus Rail LLC North America to build the connection at their meeting on Monday, Oct. 26. Construction could begin as early as next month, with completion projected in spring 2028. The Northern Columbia Basin Rail Project, designed to restore rail service that was lost in 2009, will include construction of 4.7 miles of new railroad and improvements to 2.7 miles of existing track. The port estimates it will initially generate round-trip service for 10 cars per week, growing to a daily round trip by 2045. Six companies responded to the request for bids issued in September; all six came in below the port’s estimated cost of $40 million to $47.5 million. candidates.title: WEC Lines adds fourth vessel to NWC CAI service
candidates.excerpt: WEC Lines will add a fourth vessel to its North West Continent–Canary Islands (NWC CAI) service. The expansion will strengthen connections between Northern Europe, Portugal, Spain and the Canary Islands. Following the addition, WEC Lines will operate the service with four vessels of 868 TEU each. The ships will complete a 28-day rotation. According to WEC Lines, the additional vessel will reduce operational pressure and improve schedule reliability. It will also provide greater flexibility for import and export cargo across the carrier’s short-sea network. Northbound transit times Southbound transit times WEC Lines said the enhanced service will provide consistent transit times and stronger network connectivity between Northern Europe, the Iberian Peninsula and the Canary Islands.

candidates.excerpt: Moody’s Ratings has changed the outlook on Danaos Corporation’s Ba1 Corporate Family Rating to positive from stable. The rating agency also upgraded the containership owner’s senior unsecured notes to Ba1 from Ba2. Revenue visibility supports rating action According to Danaos, Moody’s based its decision on the company’s increased revenue visibility, substantial cash position and disciplined financial management. Moody’s said these factors support strong credit metrics. They also improve Danaos’ ability to withstand weaker conditions in the containership charter market. The rating agency highlighted Danaos’ position among the world’s largest containership charter owners. It also cited the company’s long-term fixed-rate charter portfolio, positive free cash flow and focus on reducing debt before making shareholder distributions. candidates.title: Jade Pacific makes liner debut with Red Sea service
candidates.excerpt: A new Singapore-based container shipping company headed by former SeaLead executives has entered the liner trades with a service connecting India, Pakistan and Egypt’s Red Sea coast. Jade Pacific Line (JPL), established in April this year, has deployed the 1,100 teu Medkon Sia on a rotation linking Mundra, Nhava Sheva, Karachi and Sokhna before returning to Mundra. According to liner consultancy Linerlytica, the service commenced on September 25 and operates on an irregular 30- to 35-day rolling schedule rather than a fixed weekly frequency. The operation provides a direct connection between two of India’s largest container gateways, Pakistan’s principal port and Egypt’s Sokhna, which serves the Suez Canal corridor and the Egyptian hinterland. JPL is affiliated with Chinese-linked container operators Ocean Silk Line (OSL) and OVP Shipping, with OSL holding a 30% stake in the newly established company.

MSC and HMM send boxship orderbook to new peak
candidates.excerpt: MSC and HMM send boxship orderbook to new peak A flurry of new vessel orders by MSC and HMM has sent the container ship orderbook to new highs as demolition rates remain at basement levels. A further 28 container ships of more than 13,000 teu have boosted the post-2009 orderbook to a new high of 16.2m teu, 46.5% of the current fleet. An order for 20 ships of 24,000 teu by MSC at Hengli Heavy Industries in Dalian has taken the company’s orderbook for ships over 20,000 teu to 62 vessels. South Korean operator HMM has also penned an eight-ship order, worth around $1.5bn, with Hyundai Heavy Industries and HD Hyundai Samho for 13,000 teu LNG dual-fuel units. The newbuildings will be deployed on HMM’s Far East-India-Mediterranean service, said the company. candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd operated ship abandoned in Atlantic after fire Seaspan owned container ship was hit by a fire an explosion on voyage from Singapore to Brazil The Singapore-flagged container ship Espirito Santos Express suffered an explosion and fire in the Atlantic while on a voyage from Singapore – Santos. Hapag-Lloyd said in a customer advisory on 16 October that fire had been reported on the vessel. “We have been informed of the incident by Seaspan, the head owner of the vessel, with whom we remain in close contact. Seaspan has confirmed that all crew members are safe and accounted for,” the German shipping line said. Nearby vessels were reported to have responded to a distress call and the crew of the Espirito Santos Express abandoned ship. The container ship is now adrift in the Atlantic.
